parent.title: Finish the pandas 2.3.3 to 3.0.5 migration behind apache/superset#42671

shards.title: pandas 3: copy-on-write and stack changes in charts/client_processing.py
shards.why: Three sites that pandas 2.3.3 flags and pandas 3.0.5 silently changes. All 26 tests still pass on 3.0.5, which is the dangerous case: an `inplace=True` on a column selection becomes a no-op under copy-on-write and nothing fails. Fix each site as pandas' own message prescribes and keep the placeholder-replacement behaviour identical on both versions.

shards.title: pandas 3: changed API surface in pandas_postprocessing (stack, rolling quantile, loc assignment)
shards.why: Three sites that both warn on 2.3.3 and fail on 3.0.5: the new `stack` implementation rejects `dropna=`, `Rolling.quantile` renamed `quantile=` to `q=`, and `.loc[:, cols] = ...` now raises on an incompatible dtype instead of upcasting.

shards.title: pandas 3: string dtype semantics in pandas_postprocessing (aggregate, histogram, resample)
shards.why: pandas 3 infers a dedicated `str` dtype where 2.x used `object`. `mean` over a str column, `fillna(0)` into a str column, and `interpolate` on object/str now raise. Two of these three sites gave no warning on 2.3.3; the instrument cannot see this class in advance, which is why the pandas 3.0.5 run exists.

shards.title: pandas 3: 15 test expectations encode pandas 2 behaviour (human-only)
shards.why: These tests assert pandas-2 behaviour directly: `object` dtype where 3.0 infers `str`, bytes passed to `read_excel`, positional `Series[0]`, out-of-bounds datetimes coerced to NaT, groupby-apply including grouping columns. Repair sessions are not allowed to edit tests or CI config (the oracle is read-only to the agent), so this ticket is routed to a person. Until it is done, the pandas 3.0.5 unit-test job stays red even after A to D land.
